questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q01

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q01 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which presentation claim is clearest for school leaders? \

answer.text: A. School has some problems.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague.

answer.text: B. The school should provide a supervised after-school study space for students who remain on campus.

feedback.text: Correct. This claim states a clear proposal for a specific audience.

answer.text: C. People need stuff after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and unclear.

answer.text: D. My slides are about many things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q02

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q02 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which evidence best supports the claim? \

answer.text: A. Students probably need somewhere to go.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a guess.

answer.text: B. The presenter likes the idea.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal opinion.

answer.text: C. A study space sounds nice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not evidence.

answer.text: D. In a survey of 120 students, 68 reported staying on campus after dismissal at least twice a week.

feedback.text: Correct. This is specific and credible survey evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q03

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q03 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Which slide title best presents a finding? \

answer.text: A. Survey Evidence Shows Many Students Stay After School

feedback.text: Correct. This title identifies the source and finding.

answer.text: B. Things We Found

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: C. Our Presentation

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not state a finding.

answer.text: D. Random Data

feedback.text: Incorrect. This makes the evidence sound unorganized.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q04

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q04 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which speaker note best explains evidence? \

answer.text: A. This number is here because it is important.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: B. The slide already says it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The speaker should explain the evidence.

answer.text: C. Because more than half of surveyed students remain after school, the proposal addresses a need that affects many students.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains what the evidence means and connects it to the claim.

answer.text: D. I found a number in the survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This identifies source but not meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q05

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q05 [MLA.ENG2.V.01] Which sentence uses the best tone? \

answer.text: A. The proposal would provide students with a supervised academic workspace after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This is formal and precise.

answer.text: B. This would be a cool place for kids.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is casual.

answer.text: C. People should just make it happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is demanding and not academic.

answer.text: D. The thing is good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q06

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q06 [MLA.ENG2.L.01] Which sentence is grammatically correct? \

answer.text: A. Students needs a supervised study space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The plural subject needs "need."

answer.text: B. Because students need a supervised study space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment.

answer.text: C. Students need, a supervised study space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The comma is unnecessary.

answer.text: D. Students need a supervised study space.

feedback.text: Correct. The subject and verb agree.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q07

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q07 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Which revision best fits the audience of school leaders? \

answer.text: A. Kids hang around and need a place.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too informal.

answer.text: B. Students who remain after dismissal need a supervised place to complete academic work.

feedback.text: Correct. This is precise, formal, and audience-aware.

answer.text: C. This thing would help people.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: D. Everyone knows this should happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unsupported.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q08

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q08 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Which visual design choice best supports the evidence? \

answer.text: A. Tiny text with no label

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience may not understand the data.

answer.text: B. A decorative image covering the chart

feedback.text: Incorrect. This hides evidence.

answer.text: C. A readable chart with a clear title, labels, and source context

feedback.text: Correct. This helps the audience understand the evidence.

answer.text: D. Multiple unrelated animations

feedback.text: Incorrect. These distract from the message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q09

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q09 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which final review step is most important before submitting? \

answer.text: A. Check only the background color.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Readiness requires more than design.

answer.text: B. Delete the speaker notes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The oral component matters.

answer.text: C. Ignore feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Feedback should guide revision.

answer.text: D. Check that the claim, evidence, slide, speaker note, tone, and conventions align.

feedback.text: Correct. This confirms the presentation is ready to share.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q10

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q10 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] What is the purpose of an oral explanation? \

answer.text: A. To help the audience understand how evidence supports the message

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker interprets evidence and guides understanding.

answer.text: B. To repeat every slide word exactly

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral explanation should add reasoning.

answer.text: C. To avoid discussing evidence

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence should be explained.

answer.text: D. To make the presentation unrelated to the slide

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral and digital parts should align.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q11

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q11 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Why should survey size be included with the result? \

answer.text: A. It makes the slide look longer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length is not the purpose.

answer.text: B. It replaces explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence still needs explanation.

answer.text: C. It tells the audience how many people provided the data.

feedback.text: Correct. This helps the audience judge the evidence.

answer.text: D. It hides the source.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It gives more source context.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q12

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q12 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Which slide problem should be fixed first? \

answer.text: A. The slide has a clear title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is a strength, not a problem.

answer.text: B. The slide has important numbers in tiny unreadable text.

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence must be readable.

answer.text: C. The slide labels the chart.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Labels help understanding.

answer.text: D. The slide uses readable font.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Readability is a strength.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q13

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q13 [MLA.ENG2.V.01] Which revision improves formal tone? \

answer.text: A. Replace "awesome idea" with "effective proposal."

feedback.text: Correct. This changes casual wording into formal academic wording.

answer.text: B. Replace "proposal" with "thing."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is less precise.

answer.text: C. Replace "evidence" with "stuff."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal.

answer.text: D. Replace "students" with "kids hanging around."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is less formal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q14

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q14 [MLA.ENG2.L.01] Which sentence correctly uses a comma after an introductory phrase? \

answer.text: A. After dismissal many students, remain on campus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The comma is misplaced.

answer.text: B. After, dismissal many students remain on campus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This splits the phrase incorrectly.

answer.text: C. After dismissal many students remain, on campus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This comma is unnecessary.

answer.text: D. After dismissal, many students remain on campus.

feedback.text: Correct. The comma correctly follows the introductory phrase.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q15

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q15 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Feedback says the presentation does not explain why evidence matters. What should be revised? \

answer.text: A. Only the slide color

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color does not explain evidence.

answer.text: B. The file name only

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not improve the presentation.

answer.text: C. The speaker note, so it interprets the evidence and connects it to the claim

feedback.text: Correct. This directly addresses the feedback.

answer.text: D. The evidence by deleting it

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence should be explained, not removed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q16

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q16 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which presentation is publication-ready? \

answer.text: A. A presentation with clear slides but unrelated speaker notes

feedback.text: Incorrect. The parts must align.

answer.text: B. A presentation with aligned slides, clear evidence, formal notes, correct conventions, and feedback-based revision

feedback.text: Correct. This meets final readiness expectations.

answer.text: C. A presentation with evidence but many grammar errors

feedback.text: Incorrect. Conventions matter.

answer.text: D. A presentation with formal notes but unreadable slides

feedback.text: Incorrect. Digital support must be clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q17

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q17 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which transition best connects evidence to reasoning? \

answer.text: A. Anyway

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and does not show reasoning.

answer.text: B. Randomly

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not create a logical connection.

answer.text: C. This evidence matters because

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase signals that the speaker will explain the importance of the evidence.

answer.text: D. Whatever

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and dismissive.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q18

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q18 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Why should slides avoid full paragraphs of speaker text? \

answer.text: A. Full paragraphs can overload the audience and weaken the role of oral explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. Slides should highlight evidence while the speaker explains.

answer.text: B. The audience should not see any information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience should see key information.

answer.text: C. Evidence should always be hidden.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence should be clear.

answer.text: D. Paragraphs automatically prove the claim.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reasoning and evidence prove claims.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q19

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q19 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which statement correctly uses evidence? \

answer.text: A. The proposal is good because I like it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is opinion.

answer.text: B. Since 68 of 120 surveyed students stay after school, the need affects a large portion of respondents.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses specific evidence and explains meaning.

answer.text: C. Students need help because maybe they do.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is uncertain.

answer.text: D. Everyone already knows the answer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unsupported.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q20

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q20 [MLA.ENG2.L.01] Which sentence is a fragment? \

answer.text: A. Students remain after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is complete.

answer.text: B. The proposal supports students.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is complete.

answer.text: C. The survey result matters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is complete.

answer.text: D. Because the survey result matters.

feedback.text: Correct. This dependent clause does not complete the thought.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q21

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q21 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which response best uses collaborator feedback? \

answer.text: A. Feedback said the note was vague, so I revised it to explain how the evidence supports the proposal.

feedback.text: Correct. This applies feedback to a specific communication problem.

answer.text: B. Feedback said the note was vague, so I ignored it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not improve the work.

answer.text: C. Feedback said the note was vague, so I deleted the evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens the presentation.

answer.text: D. Feedback said the note was vague, so I changed an unrelated color.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not address the issue.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q22

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q22 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Which revision best improves precision? \

answer.text: A. Replace "students" with "people."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is less precise.

answer.text: B. Replace "evidence" with "stuff."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: C. Replace "a place" with "a supervised academic workspace."

feedback.text: Correct. This makes the wording more specific.

answer.text: D. Replace "proposal" with "thing."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is less precise.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q23

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q23 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which speaker note best fits a closing? \

answer.text: A. That's all I have.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not reinforce the message.

answer.text: B. I am done now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a strong academic closing.

answer.text: C. The end, I guess.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and uncertain.

answer.text: D. For these reasons, the proposal would address a documented student need after school.

feedback.text: Correct. This closing reinforces the claim and evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q24

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q24 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Which slide and note pairing is strongest? \

answer.text: A. Slide: Need. Note: This is important and stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both parts are vague.

answer.text: B. Slide: 68 of 120 surveyed students stay after school. Note: This result shows the need affects many students.

feedback.text: Correct. The slide provides evidence, and the note explains it.

answer.text: C. Slide: Random image. Note: Survey evidence matters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The slide does not support the note.

answer.text: D. Slide: Full script. Note: Same full script.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overloads the slide and repeats instead of explaining.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q25

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q25 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which final statement best describes Unit 6 mastery? \

answer.text: A. I can present a clear message using oral explanation, digital support, credible evidence, revision, and formal language.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the full Unit 6 synthesis.

answer.text: B. I can make colorful slides without evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence and explanation are required.

answer.text: C. I can read slides without explaining them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral explanation matters.

answer.text: D. I can submit without checking conventions.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Final work must be reviewed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q26

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q26 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] A student is speaking to school leaders about after-school study space. Which opening best fits the audience?\

answer.text: A. You all need to fix this right now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is demanding and not appropriate for school leaders.

answer.text: B. The hallway is annoying and everybody knows it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and vague.

answer.text: C. Thank you for considering how a supervised study space could support students who remain on campus after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This opening is respectful, clear, and audience-aware.

answer.text: D. I just want a better place because I said so.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal and unsupported.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q27

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q27 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] What is the speaker's purpose if the task says, "Explain why students need a quiet place after school"?\

answer.text: A. To entertain listeners with a funny story.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The task asks for explanation, not entertainment.

answer.text: B. To explain a student need to listeners.

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker's purpose is to explain why the study space is needed.

answer.text: C. To describe every room in the school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would not match the assigned purpose.

answer.text: D. To avoid sharing a perspective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral communication should present a clear perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q28

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q28 [MLA.ENG2.V.01] Which phrase uses the most appropriate academic vocabulary?\

answer.text: A. a supervised academic space

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase is precise and appropriate for school communication.

answer.text: B. a cool spot

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal.

answer.text: C. a good thing

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: D. some stuff after school

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q29

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q29 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which oral outline order is clearest for listeners?\

answer.text: A. Evidence, closing, opening, random fact, claim.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order is confusing.

answer.text: B. Closing, claim, opening, evidence, reasoning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Starting with the closing weakens organization.

answer.text: C. Random facts, claim, no explanation, ending.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random facts and no reasoning do not support clear oral communication.

answer.text: D. Opening, claim, evidence, reasoning, closing.

feedback.text: Correct. This order helps listeners follow the speaker's point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q30

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q30 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which source detail is most credible evidence?\

answer.text: A. A survey of 120 students reports that 68 students remain on campus after dismissal at least one day each week.

feedback.text: Correct. This is specific evidence from a stated survey.

answer.text: B. My friend says hallways are bad.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a personal comment without source support.

answer.text: C. Everybody knows students wait around.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and unsupported.

answer.text: D. I think a study space sounds nice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is an opinion, not evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q31

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q31 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which perspective is most focused for a presentation to school leaders?\

answer.text: A. The library has books, snacks are good, and hallways exist.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This mixes unrelated ideas.

answer.text: B. I like many things about school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too broad and personal.

answer.text: C. A supervised after-school study space would help students work safely while waiting on campus.

feedback.text: Correct. This is clear, focused, and audience-appropriate.

answer.text: D. Students do homework sometimes and also read novels.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a focused perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q32

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q32 [MLA.ENG2.R.07] Why should a speaker remove a detail about favorite library books from this presentation?\

answer.text: A. Books are always bad evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Books can be relevant in other presentations.

answer.text: B. It uses too many numbers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The detail does not use numbers.

answer.text: C. It is the strongest safety evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It does not address safety or study space.

answer.text: D. It does not directly support the purpose of explaining after-school study space.

feedback.text: Correct. The detail distracts from the presentation's purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q33

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q33 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Which slide heading best states a finding?\

answer.text: A. Survey

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names a source type but not the finding.

answer.text: B. Many Students Remain on Campus After Dismissal

feedback.text: Correct. This heading tells the audience what the evidence shows.

answer.text: C. Stuff About School

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

answer.text: D. Slide Two

feedback.text: Incorrect. This labels position, not meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q34

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q34 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Which visual feature best helps the audience compare survey numbers?\

answer.text: A. A busy background image.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This distracts from the numbers.

answer.text: B. Moving text on every line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This can distract the audience.

answer.text: C. A simple labeled bar chart.

feedback.text: Correct. A bar chart helps the audience compare quantities.

answer.text: D. A decorative border with no labels.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration does not clarify the evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q35

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q35 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] A slide heading says, "Stuff We Found." Which revision best improves clarity for a digital presentation about the student survey? \

answer.text: A. Survey Evidence Shows Students Need Supervised Space

feedback.text: Correct. This heading tells the audience the topic, the evidence source, and the main finding. A clear heading prepares the viewer to understand the slide.

answer.text: B. Survey Things

feedback.text: Incorrect. This heading is still vague. It does not tell what the survey showed or why the information matters.

answer.text: C. Our Project

feedback.text: Incorrect. This heading identifies that a project exists, but it does not help the audience understand the specific finding.

answer.text: D. A Colorful Student Slide

feedback.text: Incorrect. This focuses on appearance instead of the information the audience needs to understand.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q36

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q36 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which detail is the strongest evidence to include on a slide about the need for an after-school study space? \

answer.text: A. Some students probably stay after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a guess. Digital presentations need evidence that can be traced to a source or data point.

answer.text: B. Everyone knows students like places to study.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a broad claim without support. It does not provide verifiable evidence.

answer.text: C. A study space would be nice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is an opinion, not evidence. It does not show why the solution is needed.

answer.text: D. 68 of 120 surveyed students remain on campus after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This is specific, measurable evidence. It helps the audience understand the size of the need.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q37

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q37 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] A slide says, "68 of 120 students remain on campus after dismissal." Which speaker note best explains the evidence? \

answer.text: A. This number is here and it is kind of important.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This note is vague. It does not explain the meaning or importance of the evidence.

answer.text: B. This result matters because more than half of the surveyed students stay after school, so the campus has a real need for a supervised study space.

feedback.text: Correct. The note explains what the number means and connects it to the presentation purpose.

answer.text: C. The slide already says the number, so I do not need to explain it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral communication should interpret important evidence, not simply point to it.

answer.text: D. I found a number and put it on the slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This note focuses on the presenter's action instead of explaining the evidence to the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q38

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q38 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] In an integrated oral and digital presentation, what should the slide and speaker note do together? \

answer.text: A. The slide should show the key evidence, and the speaker note should explain the reasoning.

feedback.text: Correct. This creates a clear partnership between visual support and oral explanation.

answer.text: B. The slide should include every word the speaker plans to say.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A slide overloaded with text is hard to follow and weakens oral delivery.

answer.text: C. The slide should be decorative, and the speaker should provide all information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A digital slide should clarify information, not serve only as decoration.

answer.text: D. The slide and speaker note should repeat the exact same sentence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Repetition does not add explanation. The speaker should deepen the audience's understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q39

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q39 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] During rehearsal, a student notices the speaker note says only, "This is good." Which revision best improves oral explanation? \

answer.text: A. This is good and everyone should like it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is still vague and too casual for a formal presentation.

answer.text: B. The slide is blue and has a title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This describes appearance instead of explaining the message.

answer.text: C. I rehearsed and then stopped.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not revise the oral explanation.

answer.text: D. This proposal would support students who remain after dismissal by giving them a supervised place to complete academic work.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision explains the proposal, the audience need, and the reason clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q40

Question ID: ENG2_U06_UA_Q40 [MLA.ENG2.C.02] Feedback says the chart is hard to understand. Which revision best addresses the feedback? \

answer.text: A. Add a brighter background behind the chart.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A brighter background may make the data harder to read.

answer.text: B. Remove the evidence and keep the colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Removing evidence weakens the presentation.

answer.text: C. Add a clear chart title, labels, and readable numbers.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly improves the audience's ability to understand the digital evidence.

answer.text: D. Read the chart faster during the presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Speed does not solve unclear visual design.
